blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Reading an income statement at the intermediate level means going beyond the bottom line. You need to understand gross margin, operating margin and the difference between recurring revenue and one-off gains. These details tell the real story of a business.

At Czarnikow, the income statement breaks down revenue by trading desk, by product and by region. A good analyst can spot trends, compare quarters and flag anomalies before they become problems. For example, if the Brazil desk shows growing revenue but shrinking margins, that is a signal worth investigating.

The goal is not to memorise every line. The goal is to read the statement and ask the right questions: Why did this change? Is this trend sustainable? What should we do about it?

items.q: According to the text, what does reading an income statement well mean at the intermediate level?
options: Memorising every line of the statement
items.why: "going beyond the bottom line" — o resultado final sozinho não conta a história.

items.q: How does the Czarnikow income statement break down revenue?
options: By trading desk, by product and by region
items.why: "breaks down revenue by trading desk, by product and by region."

items.q: Why is a desk with growing revenue but shrinking margins worth investigating?
options: Because revenue figures are usually wrong
Because higher revenue always means lower profit
Because the desk is breaking a rule
Because it may be selling more while earning proportionally less
items.why: Inferência: receita subindo com margem caindo sugere que cada venda rende menos — um sinal a investigar.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Margins can tell a different story from revenue.
The right questions matter more than memorising lines.
A rising bottom line is proof that everything is healthy.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta justamente que o bottom line sozinho engana — margens e tendências importam.

items.q: The final questions ("Why did this change? Is this trend sustainable?") suggest that the author sees the statement mainly as…
options: a document only accountants should read
a starting point for analysis, not a conclusion
a legal record to be archived
items.why: Inferência: as perguntas mostram que o P&L abre a investigação — não a encerra.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando o novo business partner. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, pull up this month's P&L, but don't read it top to bottom just yet. I want you to see the shape first. Three product lines, three completely different stories.

Sugar looks strong — revenue is up nicely. But look at the gross margin: it has drifted down for the third month running. Whereas volume is climbing, profitability per tonne is quietly slipping. That is the P&L whispering, and it whispers long before it shouts.

Now coffee. Revenue is flat, which looks dull, but the margin is holding beautifully. While the number on the bottom line barely moves, this is actually your healthiest line. Don't let a flat top line fool you.

And ethanol — that spike? That is seasonal. Compare it to the same month last year and it disappears. A snapshot tempts you to celebrate; the comparison keeps you honest.

So here is the habit I want you to build. Never read the bottom line and stop. Read the shape, compare the periods, and trust the whisper before it becomes a shout.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie want the partner to see FIRST?
items.why: "I want you to see the shape first."

items.q: What is happening with the sugar line?
options: Revenue is flat but margin is rising
Revenue is up but gross margin has drifted down
Revenue is up and margin is holding
Revenue and margin are both falling
items.why: "revenue is up nicely. But look at the gross margin: it has drifted down."

items.q: Why does Sophie call coffee the "healthiest line" despite flat revenue?
options: Because its margin is holding well
Because it grew the most last year
Because it has no seasonal spikes
Because it has the highest revenue
items.why: "the margin is holding beautifully… this is actually your healthiest line."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "the P&L whispering, and it whispers long before it shouts"?
options: Problems show up as small early signals before they become big
The report is hard to read without help
The team talks too quietly in meetings
items.why: Inferência: o sussurro é o sinal precoce (margem escorregando) antes do problema estourar.

items.q: What is Sophie's attitude toward the ethanol spike?
options: Excited, because it proves strong growth
Cautious, because a comparison shows it is seasonal
Alarmed, because it signals a loss
Indifferent, because ethanol does not matter
items.why: Inferência: ela usa a comparação ano a ano para não se iludir com o pico sazonal — cautela, não empolgação.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Don't judge the desk on the bottom line alone." The bottom line is…
options: the first row of the report
items.why: Bottom line = resultado final (lucro/prejuízo líquido) na base do demonstrativo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Revenue rose, but the gross margin fell, so each sale earned ___ profit."
items.why: Margem bruta caindo = cada venda rende proporcionalmente menos lucro.

items.q: "This month's figure is just a snapshot." A snapshot is…
options: a single moment captured, not the full trend
items.why: Snapshot = foto de um instante; precisa de comparação para virar tendência.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The margin has ___ down slowly for three months — a small, steady decline."
items.why: Drift = deriva: movimento lento e contínuo, aqui de queda gradual.

items.q: "That surge in Q4 is just a seasonal spike." This means it is…
options: a temporary rise tied to the time of year
a drop caused by the season
items.why: Seasonal spike = pico sazonal: alta temporária ligada à época do ano.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem ao analisar um P&L. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Before we react, let's drill down into the Brazil numbers." To drill down into means to…
items.why: Drill down into = examinar em detalhe, descer aos números.

items.q: "The analyst flagged up a margin problem in the coffee desk." She…
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo.

items.q: "One-off gains can paper over a weak quarter." To paper over means to…
options: hide a problem without fixing it
items.why: Paper over = encobrir um problema sem resolvê-lo de fato.

items.q: "Let's not read too much into a single month." This means we should not…
options: interpret one figure as more significant than it is
items.why: Read too much into = tirar conclusões exageradas de um dado isolado.

items.q: "The margin trend doesn't add up." This means it…
items.why: Add up = fazer sentido, bater; aqui, os números não fecham logicamente.
